newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine 18-mth T-bill yield seen 35-40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine 18-mth T-bill yield seen 35-40 pct.

text.p: Sale of 18-month discount Treasury bills this week by Ukraine's Finance Ministry could bring in yields of 33 to 40 percent, dealers said on Monday.
"It is definite that there is interest and that auctions will take place tomorrow, and yields should be around 33 to 40 percent," said Alexander Okhrymenko, dealer at Banque Societe Generale Ukraine.
"I think there might be a compromise of 33-35 percent," said Serhiy Matveychuk of Perkombank, who added yields lower than 33 percent would not find many buyers.

Regular auctions of three-, six-, nine- and 12-month T-bills have taken place for two years but the ministry, with the central bank acting as agent, sold no 18-month-bills when it offered them in April for the first time.
Dealers said buyers of longer term paper would be mainly foreigners, with the means to invest money for the duration.
Erik Naiman, an analyst with Alpha Capital, said in a statement the long-term Treasury bills would start with yields of around 32 percent.
Naiman predicted six-month would yield around 22 percent and 12-month would yield 32 percent around the end of this month.
"This period will turn out to be one of the most difficult for the sellers of the Treasury-bills, trying to keep yields low," he said.

Yields on six-month bills auctioned last week were steady on the previous auction at 20.15 percent. Six-month bills remained at 82.61 percent, while 12-month bill yields slipped slightly to 30.46 from 30.48 percent.
Yields have more than halved since the start of the year.

Patricia Bartholomew, senior analyst at Wood and Co, predicted an increase in volumes this week because the government had to raise about 576 million hryvnias ($310 million) this week to cover T-bill payments, external debt, and a wage backlog to striking coal miners.
"That's a lot of pressure on the yields," she said. She forecast six- and nine-month yields would rise slightly and 12-month would drop a bit.
She also predicted further stability for the hryvnia, unchanged at 1.8570 on Monday on the Ukrainian Interbank Currency Exchange.
"I predict the currency would be stable, maybe a slight appreciation if foreigners are getting in on the action," she said.
